entities.summary: Marie Jean Antoine Nicolas de Caritat, Marquis of Condorcet, known as Nicolas de Condorcet, was a French philosopher, political economist, politician, and mathematician. His ideas, including support for free markets, public education, constitutional government, and equal rights for women and people of all races, and a welfare state have been said to embody the ideals of the Age of Enlightenment, of which he has been called the "last witness", and Enlightenment rationalism. As he was a critic of the constitution proposed by Marie-Jean Hérault de Séchelles in 1793, the Convention Nationale – and the Jacobin faction in particular – voted to have Condorcet arrested.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a key figure in the Age of Enlightenment, Condorcet's ideas on free markets, public education, and constitutional government influenced the development of modern democracy. His work, particularly his book 'Essai sur l'application de l'analyse à la politique' (Essay on the Application of Analysis to Politics), shaped the intellectual landscape of 18th-century Europe.
